items.title: OneLake table APIs: Now with Iceberg writes, plus richer table metadata (Preview)
items.excerpt: OneLake table APIs already let Iceberg-compatible engines discover and read tables in Microsoft Fabric. Today we're taking the next step with two additions: Iceberg REST Catalog (IRC) writes through the OneLake table endpoint, now available, and a new additional table metadata API, in preview, for adding descriptions and tags to tables and columns. Together, they make OneLake a place where any engine can not only read data, but also publish it, with the business context people and AI agents need to use it well. Write native Iceberg tables from the engines you already use Until now, the OneLake Iceberg endpoint supported read-only metadata operations. Now, IRC-compatible clients can create native Iceberg tables, commit new snapshots, and request short-lived storage credentials through the same endpoint they already use for reads. That means engines such as PyIceberg, Snowflake, and DuckDB can land results directly in OneLake using standard Iceberg tooling, with no custom connectors or copy jobs. items.title: Regular expression functions in Microsoft Fabric Data Warehouse (Preview)
items.excerpt: Data warehouses routinely ingest valuable information embedded in free text, where inconsistent structure makes it difficult to query, connect, and analyze. Incoming values can also require quality checks before they reach curated tables. Microsoft Fabric Data Warehouse and the SQL analytics endpoint now support scalar regular expression functions in preview, so you can extract useful values, validate formats, standardize text, and mask sensitive data directly in T-SQL instead of adding a separate processing step. What’s new in preview Regular expressions provide a concise way to recognize, extract, and transform complex text patterns that would otherwise require multiple string operations. The preview introduces the following scalar functions: REGEXP_LIKE : checks whether text matches a pattern. REGEXP_REPLACE : replaces matching text to clean, standardize, or mask values. REGEXP_SUBSTR : extracts a substring that matches a pattern. REGEXP_INSTR : returns the position of a matching substring. REGEXP_COUNT : counts pattern occurrences in a string. items.title: Bringing Rust-native Spark compatibility to Microsoft OneLake with Sail and LakeSail
items.excerpt: Coauthor: Shehab Amin Microsoft OneLake gives every Microsoft Fabric tenant a single, unified data lake built on open formats. One copy of data, many engines: that is the promise, and it is what makes OneLake such a strong foundation for analytics and AI alike. This post looks at how Sail , the open-source distributed compute framework, and LakeSail Cloud , the managed platform for running Sail in production, connect natively to OneLake, and what that unlocks for teams running Spark and Python workloads on Fabric. Sail is a drop-in replacement for Apache Spark, rebuilt from the ground up in Rust, with Rust-native support for Delta Lake and Apache Iceberg out of the box. That makes it a natural fit for OneLake, where lakehouse tables are stored in exactly these open formats. Point Sail at a Fabric lakehouse and it reads and writes the same tables the rest of Fabric uses, with no data copies, no extra connectors to install, and no changes to existing Spark code. One engine for data and AI Sail implements the Spark Connect protocol, the gRPC interface that decouples Spark clients from the engine that executes their plans. Existing Spark SQL and DataFrame code targeting Spark 3.5 or 4.

They use procedural logic such as conditional branches, multiple RETURN statements, or WHILE loops. Security is the natural next step, because a medallion architecture already gives you something most platforms do not: three clearly different audiences. A medallion architecture creates clear boundaries between raw, refined, and curated data. Applying security and governance at those boundaries helps reduce unnecessary exposure, simplify access decisions, and give each audience the data it needs without opening every layer.. Applications in restricted networks need real-time analytics without a route to the public internet. What is workspace-level private connectivity? Private Link is a network security feature of the Fabric platform that provides a private connection between a virtual network and Fabric. This removes the need to switch between built-in and custom modes, making SQL pool configurations easier to understand and manage consistently across the UI and APIs. items.title: Access versioned lakeFS data from Microsoft Fabric with Microsoft OneLake shortcuts
items.excerpt: Coauthor: Iddo Avneri (Treeverse) Use a live branch for up-to-date analytics or pin a shortcut to an immutable commit when reproducibility matters. Data teams often need two seemingly conflicting things: immediate access to the latest data and the ability to return to the exact data behind an earlier analysis, report, or experiment. Maintaining both typically means creating snapshots, copying datasets, or building additional pipelines. That adds operational overhead and makes it harder to know which version of the data was used. Microsoft OneLake and lakeFS provide a simpler, complementary pattern for addressing this use case. OneLake shortcuts allow Microsoft Fabric lakehouses to reference data in external storage through a unified namespace. Because lakeFS exposes versioned data through an S3-compatible gateway , Fabric can access lakeFS-managed datasets by using a OneLake S3-compatible shortcut. The result: Fabric users can access either the current data on a lakeFS branch or an immutable version from a specific commit.
